fullName.value: Bifunctional non-homologous end joining protein LigD

texts.value: With Ku forms a non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) DNA repair enzyme, which repairs dsDNA breaks with reduced fidelity (Probable). Probably involved in DNA repair during spore germination
The preference of the polymerase domain for rNTPs over dNTPs may be advantageous in dormant cells, where the dNTP pool may be limiting
Binds 3 Mn(2+); 2 Mn(2+) for polymerase/primase activity and 1 for ligase activity.
Transcriptionally regulated by SpoVT and sigma-G factor

Stationary-phase cells lacking this gene are more sensitive to ionizing radiation (IR) than cells lacking Ku (YkoV); a double mutant is not more sensitive than the ku knockout. Spores lacking this gene are more sensitive to UV, IR, ultrahigh vacuum, and dry heat
LigD has variable architecture. In Bacillus lacks the 3'-phosphoesterase domain (PE) found in Mycobacteria and some Gammaproteobacteria
In the N-terminal section; belongs to the LigD polymerase family
In the C-terminal section; belongs to the ATP-dependent DNA ligase family

DNA ligase/mRNA capping enzyme, catalytic domain

texts.value: With LigD forms a non-homologous end joining (NHEJ) DNA repair enzyme, which repairs dsDNA breaks with reduced fidelity. Binds linear dsDNA with 5'- and 3'- overhangs but not closed circular dsDNA nor ssDNA. Recruits and stimulates the ligase activity of LigD (By similarity). Probably involved in DNA repair during spore germination
Expressed in the center of the spore core, presumably with the nucleoid
Expressed in sporulating cells. Disappears after 90 minutes of spore germination
Transcriptionally regulated by SpoVT and sigma-G factor

Stationary-phase cells lacking this gene are more sensitive to ionizing radiation. Growth rate, ultraviolet light and methyl-methanesulfonate sensitivities are unaffected. The spores formed are significantly more sensitive to dry heat, high vacuum-induced desiccation, X-rays and UV radiation, but no difference in hydrogen peroxide resistance exists
Belongs to the prokaryotic Ku family
